The fresh real-device happy path inserted, bound, and completed literal IDs rice and stock (InventoryCompletionInstrumentedTest.kt:35-36,45-46,63-64), and both tests passed.

blocking_finding.smallest_reproduction: Run the focused connected test exactly as recorded; completionPersistsExactQuantitiesAndOneImmutableLogAcrossReopen succeeds using pantry IDs rice and stock, which are not UUIDs.

risks: Blocking: arbitrary strings satisfy the canonical pantry identity contract, so malformed local identity can survive Room and later conflict with the backend UUID boundary.

The recipe binding list is reduced with associateBy without first rejecting duplicate binding IDs. A malformed snapshot can therefore silently select the last duplicate binding; actual-use duplicates are rejected, but binding duplicates are not. Add an explicit uniqueness check when snapshot input becomes a trusted local record.

Version increment uses row.version + 1 with no Int.MAX_VALUE guard. This is practically remote but can wrap to Int.MIN_VALUE and weaken stale-state monotonicity if corrupt/imported data reaches the entity.

The focused tests do not directly cover InventoryNotBound, MissingActualUse, negative actual use, duplicate snapshot bindings, UUID rejection, or version overflow. Source review covers the first three main branches; the latter three remain the important adversarial gaps.
